Figma mapping review — not a prototype

This page shows how arc read the Figma frame and which existing components it proposes to build it from. It deliberately does not redraw the design.

The rendered PNG on the left is the authoritative visual reference. The right-hand column is arc's proposed node → component → token mapping, up for your review. Correct anything that's wrong before implementation starts.

Collapse these wrappers into the icon’s own size prop — don’t reproduce them as DOM nodes. Adds a lucide-react dependency if not already present.

Distilled tokens → tokens.css slots

swatches show the Figma value, label shows the proposed semantic slot
Read this first. This frame is a light, terracotta-brand consumer mobile surface. The linked tokens.css is a dark, indigo-brand developer cockpit. None of the frame's literal colour values exist in it today. The mapping below pairs each Figma value with the semantic slot it belongs in, so this screen should ship as a new theme scope — [data-theme="food-order-light"] — that re-binds those slots, rather than introducing a parallel set of variable names.

For the reviewer — ambiguities & decisions needed

arc could not resolve these from the frame alone
  1. blockingThe design system doesn't cover this frame. arc's tokens are a dark indigo cockpit; this is a light terracotta consumer app. Nothing carries over as-is. Decide: ship a new theme scope [data-theme="food-order-light"] that re-binds the existing semantic slots (arc's recommendation), or accept a second, standalone token file.
  2. blockingFonts aren't in the system. Outfit and Figtree replace Space Grotesk and Inter. Both are on Google Fonts, but this changes the app's font loading.
  3. confirmTwo colours are missing from the frame's own token list. #F3F4F6 (the most-used border in the whole design) and #FDF2EE (avatar ring) appear in the raw node data but not in the declared token set. arc recovered them from fills — please confirm they're intentional and not one-off overrides.
  4. confirmNo interaction states are designed. No hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading, empty, or error state appears anywhere in the frame — including on the primary “Order Now” button. arc proposed --brand-strong: #C85A42 as a hover value; that's an invention, not a design decision.
  5. confirmCard content order puts the heading third. Figma order inside card-body is description → tags → restaurant name → cuisine → meta. Visually distinctive, but it means the card's heading is announced after its description. arc plans a CSS order swap that keeps the visual identical while the DOM leads with the name — confirm that's acceptable.
  6. confirmThe spacer frame (89:238) is geometrically impossible. It's a 390×145 empty frame at y=70–215 that overlaps promo-banner (y=53–183). arc read it as a canvas artifact and is dropping it. If it was meant to carry real spacing, say so.
  7. confirmFree vs. paid delivery look identical. “Free Delivery” and “$2.99 Delivery” use the same 12px semibold brand treatment, so free gets no visual advantage. Intentional?
  8. confirmThe unsaved heart is a grey solid, not an outline. Card 1 = brand-filled heart (saved), card 2 = --muted-filled heart (unsaved). A filled grey heart usually reads as “disabled” rather than “not saved” — an outline heart is the conventional unsaved state.
  9. scopeOnly the collapsed/default screen is specified. No search results, no location picker list, no “See All” destination, no scroll/sticky-header behaviour, no bottom navigation, and no loading skeletons. The frame ends at 1461px with the second card — is there a bottom nav bar below the fold?
  10. scopeContent variability is unknown. Both cards happen to have exactly 3 gallery images and exactly 4 tags wrapping to 2 rows, and neither description clamps. Confirm the real bounds so GalleryStrip and the tag row are built to handle them.
  11. noteThe catalogue is aimed at a different product. Components like conversation-feed, diff-viewer, and terminal-pane are developer-tool primitives; only the generic ones (button, card, chip, badge, input, label, combobox) apply here. That's why 4 new components are needed despite a 40-component catalogue.
  12. noteThe status bar is device chrome. The “9:41 / signal / wifi / battery” row is drawn by iOS in production. arc mapped it to browser-frame for prototype fidelity only — it should not ship as product markup.
